title: Wooden Joe, Keppard and Kid Rene compared
summary: Wooden Joe was a loud blower, Keppard played more Dixie style.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well, how does Wooden Joe, say, compare with him? Does he-
Well, he was a loud blower also, Wooden Joe. Wooden Joe's a loud blower in the street.
And did Wooden Joe play a tune like he'd play it, the same method, or a different style?
Well, Wooden Joe play more a little jazzy style.
Oh, well, Keprit played more. More Dixie. More a little mixed up.
Oh, yeah. More than- Oh, yeah. That's where it started originating out from. Around Freddie.
Was he the best in his time, would you say that, or what?
Well, in that kind of jazz band, he was a little favorite of that time. He was. And after Freddie comes, uh, little René Kid René. And a little favorite player also. Them was fellas with high tones.
